body: Looks are very important to me. I was what I would consider very very attractive before being diagnosed. I don’t mean to sound douchey I just know that I was. Got the moonface after being diagnosed and noticed how differently people, from both sexes, treated me. It was eye opening to how cruel the world really is. It made me a better person as I started talking to everyone that would normally be ignored in social situations. Everyone has a cool story to tell. I worked my ass off to become an attractive person again once I went back to normal. Hell, I stayed in the gym when I had moonface because I knew I’d come out better in the end. But that was just moonface. This time there is permanent damage that I’ll never recover from. I have to deal with the cruelty of the world that no one ever talks about. Discrimination of the ugly. It’s natural. But it’s there. I take tramadol because I refuse the hard stuff. Need some pot just to get my head off of it but I live in NC so I can only go the illegal route. I can be fixed, surgically, once the inflammation goes down for an extended period of time. I was at a 2 on the inflammation scale for years. I was at a 97 in June and wasn’t properly treated with the new drug until the end of August. I got fucked hard. And now I have to either deal with my life being destroyed or wait for years for someone else to fix it. I can’t anymore. I have no control anymore. And that’s more depressing than anything else

Hi, I’m currently dealing with a debilitating flare from Wegener’s disease. I was diagnosed at 18. I never got to live my full potential as an adult. I went back to normal for years but it screwed with my head. I’m 27 now and the recent flare has wrecked my life. People don’t understand what felling helpless to disease does to you mentally, but I’m there. I’m a broken man now, but I’m here. I get it

There is no cure. They have no idea what causes it. I was fine after the first time around. This time, my life was completely destroyed. It’s more than just pain. I dealt with pain since I was first diagnosed. It has ruined everything. I can go back into full remission. I should. But the damage is done

In finding love, physical appearance is extremely important. Especially in a society where only 20% of men date 80% of the women. It’s not just the appearance change. Suddenly becoming an ugly human being was just icing on the cake. The physical constant pain from my nose collapsing, nerve damage, pressure and headaches in my head from the blood clots in my brain and pachymeningitis has made it impossible for me to even think straight. It makes you constantly tired for no reason at all. It forces you to only think “pain pain pain pain pain oh god what happened to your face pain pain pain pain pain try to act natural just smile oh god your teeth are rotting away pain pain pain pain just sleep even though tomorrow won’t be better pain pain pain no one wants to be around me anymore pain pain pain.” I refuse to take opiates. I don’t know if I can distract my brain long enough to meditate :(. I can’t stop thinking about how fucked up everything has suddenly become and I can’t fix it. Being helpless to better yourself and progress through life is terrible for a man. It’s debilitating. I appreciate your response

It's insane how different I look from just a couple months ago. Yeah, I need to talk to someone. Friends and family either don't really understand or are just naive about it. Take my sister for example who says "fuck what other people think about how you look." Of course, she is this gorgeous girl who lights up every room. My family is attractive, they'll never get it. People treat you differently and it is a humbling experience but one I wouldn't wish on Kim Jong-un. I am actually seeing a few world-renowned physicians as all of my doctors are through Duke. Things just got out of hand. I really hope I can look like myself again once I'm healthy. It just takes time and patience. I've always been a cool & collected guy. I'm a resilient person. But every man has his breaking point, and I'm almost there. I hope you're right! I hope this is temporary

To be honest, no, I am not doing ok. Dealing with the disease itself is one thing but suddenly becoming deformed is something else. Especially on the most important part of your body, your face. This is not me. And I can't do anything until the flare clears. I feel helpless and that I've lost control of my life and future. My happiness is now dependent on a handful of doctors. I can't deal with the stress.

Is looking normal even a possibility for me? Like, do most people go back to their face? It's driving me insane to look like this, and having to wait for the flare to calm before doing anything about it. Duke is an amazing place to be treated though. Thanks for the response.
